source: Gyurme Dorje (2001), Tibetan Elemental Divination Paintings, English presentation of White Beryl ff.164a–169a
authorial_boundary: Translator's summary/translation of 17th-century White Beryl; original Tibetan full wording not independently collated.

methodology_note.paraphrase: The introduction explicitly distinguishes the ordinarily destiny-element-labelled sexagenary cycle from the emphasis on corresponding vitality elements in White Beryl. Avoid assuming that the elemental mechanism is identical to a generic Chinese year pillar.

continuation_ids: TIB-R0033–TIB-R0091 (including 58 new profiles, two already logged in T03)
pitfalls: Year male/female denotes sexagenary polarity, not the native's biological sex; separate conditional male/female natives exist in some claims.
An average lifespan year is a source claim about an alleged group average, not an accurate forecast of when a person dies.
Two alternative child counts must not be credited as one exact prediction.
No stated numeric obstacle count means unknown, not zero. The special phrase 'three sets of three' is retained without forcing a scalar.
Historical demonic-cause descriptions are not medical explanations or intervention evidence.
Each entry in this single classical source is a rule statement, not an independently observed human case.
60 profiles share the 60-year year-coding dependency and cannot be treated as 60 independent predictor families.
Source does not define enough to score obstacles and many other claims objectively; no validation without a frozen operational measure.
